Bare markdown heading normalization fixture Test Author
Top-level bare heading

This top-level section is authored as a bare markdown # heading. It must lift to a canonical <section> element with a proper <section-title>, not flow through as <h1>.

Bare sub-heading with emphasis in the title

The bare ## heading lifts to <sub-section>. The emphasis in the title text must be lifted recursively — emphasis becomes <i> per the decided stylistic mapping.

Bare sub-sub-heading with inline code

Triple-hash bare heading lifts to <sub-sub-section>. Inline code in the title text must also be lifted recursively.

Top-level with strong text and strikethrough

Strong (bold) lifts to <b>; strikethrough lifts to <s> — both per the decided mappings.

Depth-4 heading passes through as <h4>

A depth-4 heading exceeds Layer 1's three section levels. It is not mapped to a section and not mapped to <b>. It passes through as a literal <h4> element with an informative diagnostic emitted.

Depth-5 heading passes through as <h5>

Same treatment as depth-4.

Depth-6 heading passes through as <h6>

Same treatment.

Bare heading inside named-tag content

An aside containing a recursive heading.

Nested bare heading inside aside content

The bare ## heading appearing inside the aside's pipe-content must also lift — the gate's walker recurses into enscribeTag content arrays.
